title: SRE Reliability, Error Budgets & Observability
description: Master SLIs, SLOs, allowable error margins, distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, and chaos engineering.

questions.question: In Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), what does an 'Error Budget' represent?
options: The allowable margin of unreliability before engineering priorities shift from features to reliability
The total financial penalty paid to cloud providers for outages
The maximum number of bugs a developer is permitted to write per sprint
The annual IT budget reserved for buying replacement hard drives

questions.question: What are the three core pillars of system Observability?
options: Metrics, Logs, and Distributed Traces
Backups, Firewalls, and Antivirus
Passwords, Keys, and Certificates
CPU, RAM, and Disk Space

questions.question: What is the difference between an SLI and an SLO?
options: An SLI is a quantifiable metric of service level; an SLO is the target objective set for that metric
An SLI is a legal contract with customers; an SLO is an internal recommendation
An SLI measures CPU utilization; an SLO measures code complexity
There is no difference; they are interchangeable terms

questions.question: What does OpenTelemetry (OTel) provide for cloud-native microservice architectures?
options: A vendor-neutral collection framework and specification for generating telemetry traces, metrics, and logs
An automated SQL database indexing engine
A load balancing proxy replacing NGINX and HAProxy
A real-time virus scanner for container images

questions.question: What is the primary goal of Chaos Engineering (e.g. Chaos Mesh, Gremlin)?
options: Proactively injecting turbulent failures into systems to reveal hidden weaknesses before outages occur
Purposely corrupting production backups to test disaster recovery speeds
Randomizing user interface button colors to test engagement
Running multiple competing versions of databases simultaneously
